Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 621 to 2076 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between The Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars The Pullman Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking November 20, 1954 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on November 20, 1954 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to December 20, 1954 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event.
